title: Internals
subject: gated-scoped-ac
summary: How the engine turns permissions and a bag into a scope or a verdict, and how the gate turns those into SQL.

axioms.text: Every resolver and verdict runs the context gate first, in memory. A context never costs a query.
A rule's target compiles to a WHERE (direct conditions) or to one id sub-query (a traversal), never both.
Rules are OR-ed, conditions within a slot AND-ed, and nothing contributing compiles to `false`.
The engine describes sub-queries and probes. The gate builds and runs them.

purpose.intro: What happens inside `createAc` and `createGatedDb`, for whoever changes them. The code is `src/engine.ts` and `src/gate.ts`; the comments there carry the reasons.

reference.statement: `resolveEffectivePermissions(roles, bag)` runs once per request, in hydration.

claims.text: The forest searched is `accountBaseline` plus `forests[orgType]`, the org type read from the bag at `orgTypePath`. No org type, no membership forest.
For each role held, the engine finds its node anywhere in that forest and collects its permissions and those of every node beneath it. A role not in the forest adds nothing.

reference.statement: `contextGate(permissions, entity, action, bag)` keeps, from the permissions the caller holds, those on this entity and action, and from each, the rules whose context passes.

claims.text: A context condition compares a bag value to its operand in memory. One without a `bag:` subject fails, and so does one where either side is unset or null, whatever the operator.
A permission with no surviving rule contributes nothing, which is why a permission declared with `rules: []` grants nothing.
Both resolvers and both verdicts start here, so a cheap refusal never reaches SQL.

reference.statement: `entityScope` compiles each surviving rule's target and combines them.

claims.text: An empty target is `true`: every row. Direct conditions are compiled by operator and column shape (drizzle's `dataType`: array, json or a single value) and AND-ed.

An operand that is unset or null compiles to the shared `false` under every operator, and the rule it sits in is dropped: it adds no rows, and no columns to the field-list union. Left to SQL, a negation against NULL would match every row or fail to parse.
A traversal becomes an `IdSubquery`: select `id` from the entity, inner-joined to the far entity on the condition's column and `on`, filtered by its `where`.
The WHEREs are OR-ed into `base`; any rule that is `true` makes `base` `true`; none makes it `false`. Sub-queries are kept in a list beside it.
Field lists union across contributing permissions; any one without a list means every column (`fields: undefined`).

reference.statement: On a read only, each `visibilityJoins[entity]` entry `{ via, fk }` adds a sub-query: the `fk` column of the `via` rows the caller may read.

claims.text: The channel is built from the `via` entity's `base` alone. A traversal in a rule on the `via` entity does not carry into the channel.

reference.statement: A scope is `{ base, idSubqueries, fields }` cast to `Scope<entity, action>`.

claims.text: The brand is a type-only `unique symbol`: no key is ever written at runtime. The cast in `scopeFor` is the only mint.

reference.statement: Create and update also answer with a `Verdict`, `{ allow, reason?, requires? }`, taken before anything is written.

claims.text: `allowUpdate(permissions, entity, body, bag)`: no permission passing context denies. One passing permission without a field list allows every column. Otherwise every key of `body` must be in the union of their lists, and the reason names the ones that are not.

`allowCreate(permissions, entity, bag)`: a rule with no payload allows outright. A payload's direct conditions are settled in memory; a payload traversal becomes an `ExistsProbe` on the joined entity, keyed by the bag value, with its `where` AND-ed in. An absent value anywhere the rule reads (either side of a direct condition, the traversal's subject, an operand in its `where`) makes the rule deny without a query.
Any rule allowing outright wins. Otherwise the probes come back as `requires`, OR-ed: the create proceeds if any one finds a row. With neither, the create is denied.

reference.statement: `createGatedDb` turns a scope into SQL on the raw handle and runs it. No other module touches the handle.

claims.text: `scopeWhere` assembles `base OR <pk> IN (sub-query) OR …`, one `IN` per described sub-query, building each as a drizzle select on the raw handle.
`read` selects the scope's `fields` (or every column) under that WHERE, AND-ed with the caller's narrowing; `count` reuses the WHERE without paging.
`update` and `delete` fuse `<pk> = id AND scopeWhere` into the statement and return what `RETURNING` gives, or `null`. The write probes run the same WHERE as a select.

`create` takes the verdict with `requestBody` set to the values, runs the probes one at a time until one finds a row, then inserts. The check and the insert are not one statement, a window the code accepts and states.
`idColumns` sets the primary key for the outer `<pk> = id` and `<pk> IN (…)`. A traversal's sub-query always selects the entity's `id`.

reference.statement: `createAc` walks every permission's target conditions, the ones inside a traversal's `where` included, and throws when `is` or `isNot` points at an array or json column.

claims.text: It runs in the engine because `config.ts` has no tables. An entity missing from `tables` is skipped and stays a request-time error.
